Proper scores for quantile predictions

Source: R/pred-score.R
wgh_score.Rd

Scores a matrix of predicted quantiles against observations: mean pinball loss over the grid, the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), the weighted interval score built from the 50%, 80% and 90% central intervals and the median, empirical coverage and mean width of those intervals, and the absolute error of the median.

Usage

wgh_score(obs, qmat, taus)

Arguments

obs

Observed values.

qmat

Matrix of predicted quantiles (one column per quantile).

taus

The quantiles of the columns.

Value

A one-row tibble.

Details

The CRPS equals twice the integral of the pinball loss over all quantile levels between 0 and 1. It is approximated with the trapezoid rule over the supplied grid: the loss is interpolated linearly between adjacent quantiles, and in the tails below the lowest and above the highest quantile it is taken to fall linearly to zero. Each quantile is therefore weighted by the spacing of its neighbours, so unevenly spaced grids such as c(0.03, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.97) are scored correctly. Because the tails are approximated, the CRPS of a short grid is a slight underestimate, and the same grid should be used for every model being compared. pinball is the plain mean over the grid.

Examples

set.seed(1); y <- rnorm(200)
taus <- c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95)
Q <- matrix(qnorm(taus), 200, 7, byrow = TRUE)
wgh_score(y, Q, taus)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   pinball  crps mae_median coverage_50 width_50 coverage_80 width_80 coverage_90
#>     <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1   0.212 0.506      0.739        0.55     1.35        0.82     2.56       0.925
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: width_90 <dbl>, wis <dbl>
